content.text:
The evidence has two conflicting ledgers, from Tenant 3 and Tenant 4. Neither one gives billed and payment figures, so the rule can't be applied directly. The two sources disagree about which invoice is largest.

Tenant 3 lists balances for all four invoices and says Harbor Printing is the largest, at 3,600. Tenant 4 says Delta Cleaning is the largest at 5,200 "after the audit correction," and it gives no balances for the other invoices. The Tenant 4 note is a correction, so it may be the more recent and authoritative source. The other sentences in that note (printer serviced, month end on a Friday) are irrelevant.

The two ledgers might also belong to different tenants and cover different invoices. In that case Delta Cleaning is 3,000 in Tenant 3 but 5,200 in Tenant 4, which would be inconsistent unless a correction changed it. The audit correction is the likely explanation for the change. So Delta Cleaning at 5,200 is larger than Harbor Printing at 3,600.

**C**
